text: On October 15 condition `ownership-runtime-values-20261015-f78d995f`, interpreting all 2,658 changed ownership row observations over 949 storage keys as sets of Ruby values yields 764 with no runtime-set change, 328 storage-cell additions/removals, two widenings and 1,564 narrowings. Of the narrowings, 578 exclude a value CRuby produces and measured main admits, 900 agree with finite runtime witnesses, 57 are justified by source guards, 16 are boundary-only unset-ivar cases and 13 remain unwitnessed. Independent review upholds the 578/900 recount with the `respond_to` causal explanation corrected, confirms 10/10 sampled counterexamples and reruns all 35 original observations on CRuby 4.0.7. These are repeated observations across schedules and cache/IR/return cells, not 578 independent defects. Measured main `f78d995f` types `render`, `redirect_to` and `respond_to` as `nil`. This model is already too narrow at 15 Forem helpers and three Mastodon error helpers. The excluded-value and witness-consistent families carry the same module-side Unresolved evidence, so this evidence provides no ownership rule that keeps only the sound narrowings. Persistence, transaction, account, rendering and format-collector doubles are explicit; supplemental actual Rails components confirm sampled HTML/API String returns, with account/template fixtures retained. Boundary witnesses do not establish live-request reachability, and witness consistency is not universal soundness. No integration design is published as confirmed.
verdict: Upheld finite runtime classification and excluded-value witnesses.
